:::{#exm-rule-of-inference}
#### A pattern that is not a rule of inference
<!-- no-figure: the truth table row is the display -->

The pattern

$$
\frac{P \Rightarrow Q, \quad Q}{P}
$$

is not a [rule of inference](#def-rule-of-inference).
In the row of the [truth table](#def-truth-table) where $P$ is false and $Q$ is true,
both [premises](#def-premise) are true,
by the definition of [implies](#def-implies),
but the [conclusion](#def-conclusion) $P$ is false.
For example, "if $n = 2$, then $n$ is [even](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd)" and "$n$ is even"
are both true for $n = 4$,
but "$n = 2$" is false.

:::
